input.quote: 4.9 The members of the PG shall not be liable to any other Party or to each other for any loss or damage sustained by reason of a Supplier's failure to perform in accordance with the terms and conditions of its Supply Contract, or as a result of APCN 2 not meeting the RFPA Date as specified in the Supply Contract, or if APCN 2 does not perform in accordance with the technical specifications and other requirements of the Supply Contract, or APCN 2 is not integrated or placed into operation. The Parties recognize and agree that the PG does not make any representations or warranties
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no express performance or conformance warranty anywhere. Paragraph 4.9 (p0126) is a двух-layered exclusion: its first sentence excludes PG liability "for any loss or damage" where APCN 2 "does not perform in accordance with the technical specifications and other requirements of the Supply Contract, or APCN 2 is not integrated or placed into operation," and its second sentence disclaims all representations and warranties, extended by p0127 to Supplier performance, Wet Segment performance/reliability and integration, with "nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as such a warranty or guarantee." Paragraphs 4.6-4.8 (p0122-p0125) only oblige the PG to procure Supply Contract terms and permit the PG to pursue the Supplier; they give the Parties no warranty and no remedy. Paragraph 10.1-10.2 (p0169-p0171) is a reasonable-efforts "efficient working order" maintenance covenant, not a conformance warranty. That is the walk-away position and fails every fallback element. We target the fallback and insert numbered Paragraph 4.10: a 90-day Wet Segment/software conformance warranty against documentation and the Supply Contract specifications, a 30-day services warranty covering services performed by the PG under this Agreement, and repair, replacement or refund at the affected Party's election. Critically, the carve-out is now placed in the first sentence of 4.9 as well as in the disclaimer sentence and the (i)-(iii) tail, because repair, replacement and refund are forms of liability that the retained no-liability sentence would otherwise defeat; the express "4.10" numbering makes all three cross-references resolve. Every other word of 4.9 and p0127 is retained verbatim. Paragraph 25 (p0260) already carries a mutual compliance-with-law covenant, a preferred-level element only, not required at the fallback we selected.

proposal.summary: Add numbered Paragraph 4.10 giving a 90-day Wet Segment/software conformance warranty, a 30-day services warranty and repair/replacement or refund remedies, and carve it out of both the liability exclusion and the warranty disclaimer in Paragraph 4.9.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Paragraph 4.9 both excludes PG liability for APCN 2 failing to meet the Supply Contract specifications and disclaims all warranties, which is our walk-away position, so we have added Paragraph 4.10 with a short fallback conformance warranty (90 days for the Wet Segment and its software against its documentation, 30 days for services) and repair, replacement or refund as the remedy. We have carved Paragraph 4.10 out of the liability exclusion as well as the disclaimer so the remedy is not swallowed by the retained language.

ops.text: 4.10 The PG warrants that (a) for a period of ninety (90) days following the RFPA Date, the Wet Segment and any software delivered with it will conform to its documentation and to the technical specifications and other requirements of the Supply Contract, and (b) for a period of thirty (30) days following their performance, services performed by the PG under this Agreement will conform to the requirements of this Agreement. For breach of this warranty the PG shall, as the affected Party elects, repair or replace the non-conforming Wet Segment, software or services, or refund the amounts paid by that Party in respect of the non-conforming item.
